# Introduction

This vignette provides an _overview_ of how to use the functions in the 
__catalytic__ package that focuses on commonalities. The other __catalytic__ 
vignettes go into the particularities of each of the individual model-estimating
functions.

The goal of the __catalytic__ package is to build framework for catalytic prior distributions, as proposed in the paper "Catalytic prior distributions with application to generalized linear models" by Huang et al. Stabilizing high-dimensional working models by shrinking them towards simplified models. This is achieved by supplementing observed data with weighted synthetic data generated from a predictive distribution under the simpler model.


```{r catalytic-mle, eval=TRUE}
swim_data <- readRDS("~/catalytic/data/swim_data.rds")

swim_glm_1 <- glm(emp1y ~ FEMALE + AGEGE35 + NUMCHILD, data = swim_data, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

coef(summary(swim_glm_1))
```
# Step 1: Initialization

```{r initilization }
data_ <- initialization(
  formula = emp1y ~ FEMALE,
  data = swim_data,
  syn_size = 5000
)

data_
```
`data_` cantains all the information about data, especially about synthetic and observation data, so you don't need to re-enter the synthetic data information in following steps.

```{r show data_}
names(data_)
```

# Step 2.1: Fit - point estimate for tau

As mentioned before, the object `data_` is from function `initialization` in Step 1. `data_` will cover similar job as the `data` from `stats::glm`.

```{r point estimate }
# Get point estimate from defined single tau
point_estimate_result <- cat_tau_glm(
  formula = emp1y ~ FEMALE + AGEGE35 + NUMCHILD,
  data_ = data_,
  tau = ncol(data_$data) / 4
)

point_estimate_result
```

# Step 2.2: Fit - freqentist priors

```{r freqentist }
freq_result <- cat_freq_glm(
  formula = emp1y ~ FEMALE + AGEGE35 + NUMCHILD,
  data_ = data_,
  risk_estimate_method = "parametric_bootstrap",
  discrepancy_function = "square_error"
)

freq_result
```
